claim: Mcm2 is a subunit of the minichromosome maintenance proteins 2–7 (Mcm2-7) helicase.
source: Mcm2, a subunit of the minichromosome maintenance proteins 2–7 (Mcm2-7) helicase best known for its role in DNA replication, contains a histone binding motif that facilitates the transfer of parental histones following DNA replication.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is established knowledge about Mcm2.

claim: Mcm2 contains a histone binding motif that facilitates the transfer of parental histones following DNA replication.
source: Mcm2, a subunit of the minichromosome maintenance proteins 2–7 (Mcm2-7) helicase best known for its role in DNA replication, contains a histone binding motif that facilitates the transfer of parental histones following DNA replication.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Mcm2 is important for the differentiation of mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells.
source: Here, we show that Mcm2 is important for the differentiation of mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The Mcm2-2A mutation defective in histone binding shows defects in silencing of pluripotent genes.
source: The Mcm2-2A mutation defective in histone binding shows defects in silencing of pluripotent genes and the induction of lineage-specific genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RT-PCR and RNA-seq data in the manuscript.

claim: The Mcm2-2A mutation shows defects in the induction of lineage-specific genes.
source: The Mcm2-2A mutation defective in histone binding shows defects in silencing of pluripotent genes and the induction of lineage-specific genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RT-PCR and RNA-seq data in the manuscript.

claim: The defects in the induction of lineage-specific genes in Mcm2-2A mutant cells are likely, at least in part, due to reduced binding to Asf1a.
source: The defects in the induction of lineage-specific genes in the mutant cells are likely, at least in part, due to reduced binding to Asf1a, a histone chaperone that binds Mcm2 and is important for nucleosome disassembly at bivalent chromatin domains containing repressive H3K27me3 and active H3K4me3 modifications during differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by genetic epistasis experiments and transcriptome analysis.

claim: Asf1a is a histone chaperone that binds Mcm2.
source: The defects in the induction of lineage-specific genes in the mutant cells are likely, at least in part, due to reduced binding to Asf1a, a histone chaperone that binds Mcm2 and is important for nucleosome disassembly at bivalent chromatin domains containing repressive H3K27me3 and active H3K4me3 modifications during differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by previous literature cited in the manuscript.

claim: Asf1a is important for nucleosome disassembly at bivalent chromatin domains containing repressive H3K27me3 and active H3K4me3 modifications during differentiation.
source: The defects in the induction of lineage-specific genes in the mutant cells are likely, at least in part, due to reduced binding to Asf1a, a histone chaperone that binds Mcm2 and is important for nucleosome disassembly at bivalent chromatin domains containing repressive H3K27me3 and active H3K4me3 modifications during differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by previous work cited in the manuscript (Gao et al., 2018).

claim: Mcm2 localizes at transcription starting sites.
source: Mcm2 localizes at transcription starting sites and the binding of Mcm2 at gene promoters is disrupted in both Mcm2-2A ES cells and neural precursor cells (NPCs).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by CUT&RUN data in the manuscript.

claim: The binding of Mcm2 at gene promoters is disrupted in both Mcm2-2A ES cells and neural precursor cells (NPCs).
source: Mcm2 localizes at transcription starting sites and the binding of Mcm2 at gene promoters is disrupted in both Mcm2-2A ES cells and neural precursor cells (NPCs).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by CUT&RUN data in the manuscript.

claim: Reduced Mcm2 binding at bivalent chromatin domains in Mcm2-2A ES cells correlates with decreased chromatin accessibility at corresponding sites in NPCs.
source: Reduced Mcm2 binding at bivalent chromatin domains in Mcm2-2A ES cells correlates with decreased chromatin accessibility at corresponding sites in NPCs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by CUT&RUN and ATAC-seq data in the manuscript.

claim: ES cells are pluripotent cells that possess both the ability to self-renew and the potential to differentiate into lineage-specific cell types.
source: Embryonic stem (ES) cells (ESCs) are pluripotent cells that possess both the ability to self-renew and the potential to differentiate into lineage-specific cell types (De Los Angeles et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: During mouse ESC differentiation, pluripotency genes such as Pou5f1, Sox2, and Nanog are silenced.
source: During mouse ESC differentiation, pluripotency genes such as Pou5f1, Sox2, and Nanog are silenced, whereas lineage-specific genes are up-regulated (Sha and Boyer, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: During mouse ESC differentiation, lineage-specific genes are up-regulated.
source: During mouse ESC differentiation, pluripotency genes such as Pou5f1, Sox2, and Nanog are silenced, whereas lineage-specific genes are up-regulated (Sha and Boyer, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The silencing of pluripotency genes (Pou5f1, Sox2, and Nanog) is associated with both a dramatic reduction of tri-methylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) and an increase in H3K27me3.
source: For instance, the silencing of pluripotency genes (Pou5f1, Sox2, and Nanog) is associated with both a dramatic reduction of tri-methylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3), a histone modification associated with active gene transcription, and an increase in H3K27me3, a repressive histone modification (Atlasi and Stunnenberg, 2017; Mikkelsen et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: H3K4me3 is a histone modification associated with active gene transcription.
source: For instance, the silencing of pluripotency genes (Pou5f1, Sox2, and Nanog) is associated with both a dramatic reduction of tri-methylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3), a histone modification associated with active gene transcription, and an increase in H3K27me3, a repressive histone modification (Atlasi and Stunnenberg, 2017; Mikkelsen et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge in the field.

claim: H3K27me3 is a repressive histone modification.
source: For instance, the silencing of pluripotency genes (Pou5f1, Sox2, and Nanog) is associated with both a dramatic reduction of tri-methylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3), a histone modification associated with active gene transcription, and an increase in H3K27me3, a repressive histone modification (Atlasi and Stunnenberg, 2017; Mikkelsen et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is established knowledge in the field.

claim: The promoters of lineage-specific genes are marked by both repressive H3K27me3 and active H3K4me3 marks.
source: In contrast, the promoters of lineage-specific genes, which are marked by both repressive H3K27me3 and active H3K4me3 marks, needs to be resolved for silencing and/or induction of lineage-specific genes during differentiation (Bernstein et al., 2006; Harikumar and Meshorer, 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: CAF-1 is a histone chaperone involved in the deposition of newly synthesized H3-H4 onto replicating DNA.
source: For instance, chromatin assembly factor 1 (CAF-1), a histone chaperone involved in the deposition of newly synthesized H3-H4 onto replicating DNA, is important for cell fate maintenance (Ishiuchi et al., 2015; Smith and Stillman, 1989).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: CAF-1 is important for cell fate maintenance.
source: For instance, chromatin assembly factor 1 (CAF-1), a histone chaperone involved in the deposition of newly synthesized H3-H4 onto replicating DNA, is important for cell fate maintenance (Ishiuchi et al., 2015; Smith and Stillman, 1989).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Depletion of subunits of the CAF-1 complex in embryonic fibroblasts results in increased reprogramming efficiency into iPSC cells.
source: Depletion of subunits of the CAF-1 complex in embryonic fibroblasts results in increased reprogramming efficiency into iPSC cells (Cheloufi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: In ESCs, CAF-1 depletion leads to an increase in the percentage of 2C-like cells.
source: In ESCs, CAF-1 depletion leads to an increase in the percentage of 2C-like cells (2-cell-stage embryos), as well as defects in differentiation (Cheng et al., 2019; Ishiuchi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: In ESCs, CAF-1 depletion leads to defects in differentiation.
source: In ESCs, CAF-1 depletion leads to an increase in the percentage of 2C-like cells (2-cell-stage embryos), as well as defects in differentiation (Cheng et al., 2019; Ishiuchi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Asf1a regulates the disassembly of nucleosomes at bivalent chromatin domains for the induction of lineage-specific genes.
source: In contrast, Asf1a, a histone chaperone involved in the delivery of newly synthesized H3-H4 to CAF-1 in replication-coupled nucleosome assembly, as well as to HIRA, a histone chaperone involved in replication-independent (RI) nucleosome assembly (De Koning et al., 2007; English et al., 2006; Tagami et al., 2004), regulates the disassembly of nucleosomes at bivalent chromatin domains for the induction of lineage-specific genes (Gao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Histone chaperone CAF-1 promotes the formation of H3K27me3-mediated silencing at pluripotent genes.
source: Moreover, histone chaperone CAF-1 promotes the formation of H3K27me3-mediated silencing at pluripotent genes (Cheng et al., 2019), whereas HIRA facilitates the PRC2 silencing complex at developmental loci during differentiation (Banaszynski et al., 2013; Ray-Gallet et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: HIRA facilitates the PRC2 silencing complex at developmental loci during differentiation.
source: Moreover, histone chaperone CAF-1 promotes the formation of H3K27me3-mediated silencing at pluripotent genes (Cheng et al., 2019), whereas HIRA facilitates the PRC2 silencing complex at developmental loci during differentiation (Banaszynski et al., 2013; Ray-Gallet et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Pole3 and Pole4 are two subunits of leading strand DNA polymerase ε that interact with H3-H4 and facilitate the transfer of parental histones to leading strands of DNA replication forks in both yeast and mouse ESCs.
source: Pole3 and Pole4, two subunits of leading strand DNA polymerase ε, interact with H3-H4 and facilitate the transfer of parental histones to leading strands of DNA replication forks in both yeast and mouse ESCs (Li et al., 2020; Yu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Mcm2 contains a histone binding domain (HBD).
source: On the other hand, Mcm2, a subunit of the minichromosome maintenance proteins 2–7 (Mcm2-7) complex that plays an essential role in DNA replication as the replicative helicase (Tye, 1999), contains a histone binding domain (HBD) (Huang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Mutations at HBDs (Y81A and Y90A) of Mcm2 (Mcm2-2A) in both yeast and mouse ESCs leads to defects in the transfer of parental histones to lagging strands of DNA replication forks.
source: Mutations at HBDs (Y81A and Y90A) of Mcm2 (Mcm2-2A) in both yeast and mouse ESCs leads to defects in the transfer of parental histones to lagging strands of DNA replication forks (Gan et al., 2018; Li et al., 2020; Petryk et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Mcm2 interacts with Asf1 that is bridged by H3-H4 proteins.
source: Moreover, Mcm2 interacts with Asf1 that is bridged by H3-H4 proteins (Groth et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Mcm2 interacts with the carboxyl-terminal domain of RNA Pol II in Xenopus oocytes.
source: Besides its functions in DNA replication and histone deposition, Mcm2 also interacts with the carboxyl-terminal domain of RNA Pol II in Xenopus oocytes, and the Mcm2-7 complex is required for RNA Pol II-mediated transcription at some settings in mammalian cells (Snyder et al., 2009; Yankulov et al., 1999), indicating a possible role of Mcm2 in gene transcription.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The Mcm2-7 complex is required for RNA Pol II-mediated transcription at some settings in mammalian cells.
source: Besides its functions in DNA replication and histone deposition, Mcm2 also interacts with the carboxyl-terminal domain of RNA Pol II in Xenopus oocytes, and the Mcm2-7 complex is required for RNA Pol II-mediated transcription at some settings in mammalian cells (Snyder et al., 2009; Yankulov et al., 1999), indicating a possible role of Mcm2 in gene transcription.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Mouse ESCs with deletion of Pole3 and Pole4 or mutations at the HBD of Mcm2 grow normally and maintain stemness.
source: Mouse ESCs with deletion of Pole3 and Pole4 or mutations at the HBD of Mcm2 grow normally and maintain stemness.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by data in the manuscript.

claim: All mutants (Pole3 KO, Pole4 KO, Mcm2-2A, Mcm2-2A Pole3 KO, Mcm2-2A Pole4 KO) exhibited reduced EB size at day 9 compared to wild type cells.
source: We observed that all mutants exhibited reduced EB size at day 9 compared to wild type (WT) cells, with Mcm2-2A, Mcm2-2A Pole3 KO, Mcm2-2A Pole4 KO double mutant cells exhibiting dramatic defects based on morphology (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by images in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Mcm2-2A, Mcm2-2A Pole3 KO, Mcm2-2A Pole4 KO double mutant cells exhibited dramatic defects in EB formation based on morphology.
source: We observed that all mutants exhibited reduced EB size at day 9 compared to wild type (WT) cells, with Mcm2-2A, Mcm2-2A Pole3 KO, Mcm2-2A Pole4 KO double mutant cells exhibiting dramatic defects based on morphology (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by images in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The silencing of Pou5f1 was compromised in all the mutant cells.
source: Similarly, we observed that the silencing of Pou5f1, a gene involved in pluripotency, was compromised in all the mutant cells, with the Mcm2-2A Pole3 KO and Mcm2-2A Pole4 KO double mutant cells showing larger effects than either single mutant alone (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The Mcm2-2A Pole3 KO and Mcm2-2A Pole4 KO double mutant cells showed larger effects on Pou5f1 silencing than either single mutant alone.
source: Similarly, we observed that the silencing of Pou5f1, a gene involved in pluripotency, was compromised in all the mutant cells, with the Mcm2-2A Pole3 KO and Mcm2-2A Pole4 KO double mutant cells showing larger effects than either single mutant alone (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The transcription of several lineage-specific genes was delayed in all the mutant cells.
source: Finally, the transcription of several lineage-specific genes, representing three germ layers, was delayed in all the mutant cells, with the double mutants showing the strongest defects (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The double mutants (Mcm2-2A Pole3 KO and Mcm2-2A Pole4 KO) showed the strongest defects in transcription of lineage-specific genes.
source: Finally, the transcription of several lineage-specific genes, representing three germ layers, was delayed in all the mutant cells, with the double mutants showing the strongest defects (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Mcm2-2A mutant and WT cells showed similarly low frequencies of 2C-like cells.
source: We found that Mcm2-2A mutant and WT cells showed similarly low frequencies of 2C-like cells (Figure 1D and E), indicating that ESC plasticity is not altered in Mcm2-2A mutant cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1D and E.

claim: ESC plasticity is not altered in Mcm2-2A mutant cells.
source: We found that Mcm2-2A mutant and WT cells showed similarly low frequencies of 2C-like cells (Figure 1D and E), indicating that ESC plasticity is not altered in Mcm2-2A mutant cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results and inferred from the 2C-like cell frequency data.

claim: Mcm2-2A and double mutant (Mcm2-2A and Pole4 KO) cells exhibited compromised silencing of Pou5f1 and Nanog during neural differentiation.
source: Consistent with the EB formation assays, Mcm2-2A and double mutant (Mcm2-2A and Pole4 KO) cells exhibited compromised silencing of Pou5f1 and Nanog as well as defects in the induction of Sox21 and Pax6 expression (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Mcm2-2A and double mutant (Mcm2-2A and Pole4 KO) cells exhibited defects in the induction of Sox21 and Pax6 expression during neural differentiation.
source: Consistent with the EB formation assays, Mcm2-2A and double mutant (Mcm2-2A and Pole4 KO) cells exhibited compromised silencing of Pou5f1 and Nanog as well as defects in the induction of Sox21 and Pax6 expression (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Pole4 KO had no significant effects on the expression of pluripotency genes or neural lineage genes compared with WT cells during neural differentiation.
source: In contrast, Pole4 KO had no significant effects on the expression of pluripotency genes or neural lineage genes compared with WT cells during neural differentiation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: From day 7 to day 9 of neural differentiation, a dramatic loss of GFP expression was observed in WT cells, whereas ~30% of Mcm2-2A cells preserved GFP signals at day 9.
source: Interestingly, from day 7 to day 9, we observed a dramatic loss of GFP expression in WT cells, whereas ~30% of Mcm2-2A cells preserved GFP signals at day 9 (Figure 2B and C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by FACS analysis in Figure 2B and C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Higher expression level of Pou5f1 and Nanog proteins were detected in Mcm2-2A cells compared to WT cells after differentiation.
source: Accordingly, we detected higher expression level of Pou5f1 and Nanog proteins in Mcm2-2A cells compared to WT cells after differentiation (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 2D.

claim: Mcm2-2A cells upon differentiation did not exhibit neural cell morphology like WT cells.
source: Finally, Mcm2-2A cells upon differentiation did not exhibit neural cell morphology like WT cells (Figure 2B), providing additional support to the idea that the Mcm2-2A mutation compromises the differentiation of mouse ESCs.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by images in Figure 2B.

claim: Expression of WT Mcm2 in Mcm2-2A cells led to silencing of Pou5f1 to a similar degree as WT cells.
source: Gene expression analysis by RT-PCR indicated that expression of WT Mcm2 in Mcm2-2A cells led to silencing of Pou5f1 to a similar degree as WT cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-PCR data.

claim: Expression of Mcm2 partially rescued the defects in the expression of lineage-specific genes in Mcm2-2A.
source: Interestingly, expression of Mcm2 partially rescued the defects in the expression of lineage-specific genes in Mcm2-2A (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 2G.

claim: The Mcm2-Asf1 interaction is reduced in Mcm2-2A cells.
source: Mcm2 interacts with histone chaperone Asf1, which is bridged by H3-H4 (Huang et al., 2015). Consequently, the Mcm2-Asf1 interaction is reduced in Mcm2-2A cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by a citation.

claim: Deletion of Asf1a, but not Asf1b, in mouse ESCs impairs the induction of lineage-specific genes.
source: We have shown that deletion of Asf1a, but not Asf1b, in mouse ESCs impairs the induction of lineage-specific genes (Gao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by a citation.

claim: Asf1a overexpression could not rescue the defects in differentiation of Mcm2-2A cells.
source: To understand how Mcm2-2A affects differentiation, we first overexpressed Asf1a in Mcm2-2A cells and found that Asf1a overexpression could not rescue the defects in differentiation of Mcm2-2A cells based on analysis of cell morphology (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B) and the expression of Pou5f1 and lineage-specific genes (Sox21 and Pax6) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-E.

claim: Mcm2-2A Asf1a KO double mutant exhibited similar morphology as Mcm2-2A cells but not Asf1a KO cells after differentiation.
source: We observed that Mcm2-2A Asf1a KO double mutant exhibited similar morphology as Mcm2-2A cells but not Asf1a KO cells after differentiation (Figure 2—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by images in Figure 2—figure supplement 2H.

claim: Asf1a KO dramatically reduced the induction of lineage-specific genes, while having little effects on the silencing of Pou5f1.
source: As reported, Asf1a KO dramatically reduced the induction of lineage-specific genes, while having little effects on the silencing of Pou5f1 (Gao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by a citation.

claim: Both Mcm2-2A cell line and Mcm2-2A Asf1a KO double mutant cell line showed compromised silencing of Pou5f1.
source: In contrast, both Mcm2-2A cell line and Mcm2-2A Asf1a KO double mutant cell line showed compromised silencing of Pou5f1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2I.

claim: Mcm2-2A Asf1a KO double mutant cells did not show additional defects in the induction of lineage-specific genes compared with Mcm2-2A or Asf1a KO single mutant alone.
source: On the other hand, while significant defects in the induction of neural lineage gene expression (Pax6 and Sox21) were detected in either Mcm2-2A cells or Asf1a KO cells, Mcm2-2A Asf1a KO double mutant cells did not show additional defects in the induction of lineage-specific genes compared with Mcm2-2A or Asf1a KO single mutant alone (Figure 2—figure supplement 2I),
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2I.

claim: Mcm2-2A mutant suppressed the defects in the induction of Zfpm2 in Asf1a KO cells.
source: Interestingly, we observed that Mcm2-2A mutant suppressed the defects in the induction of another neural lineage marker, Zfpm2 in Asf1a KO cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2I.

claim: The Mcm2-2A mutation caused greater gene expression changes in NPCs than in ESCs, with 54 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between WT and Mcm2-2A ESCs and 609 DEGs between WT and Mcm2-2A NPCs.
source: In general, the Mcm2-2A mutation caused greater gene expression changes in NPCs than in ESCs, with 54 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between WT and Mcm2-2A ESCs and 609 DEGs between WT and Mcm2-2A NPCs (false discovery rate<0.01, |log2 fold change|>1) (Figure 3A), providing an explanation for the observation that the Mcm2-2A mutation does not affect stemness or proliferation of mouse ESCs dramatically.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by RNA-seq data in Figure 3A.

claim: 352 down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A NPCs were enriched in neurodevelopment, such as forebrain/hindbrain development and neural nucleus development.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis of 352 down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A NPCs were enriched in neurodevelopment, such as forebrain/hindbrain development and neural nucleus development (Figure 3D), whereas 238 up-regulated genes compared to WT ESCs were related to stem cell population maintenance (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by GO analysis in Figure 3D.

claim: 238 up-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A NPCs compared to WT ESCs were related to stem cell population maintenance.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis of 352 down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A NPCs were enriched in neurodevelopment, such as forebrain/hindbrain development and neural nucleus development (Figure 3D), whereas 238 up-regulated genes compared to WT ESCs were related to stem cell population maintenance (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by GO analysis in Figure 3E.

claim: Most of the down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs (62% of total) were overlapped with the down-regulated genes in Asf1a KO NPCs.
source: Interestingly, we observed that most of the down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs (62% of total), which represent those genes showing defects in induction compared to WT NPC, were overlapped with the down-regulated genes in Asf1a KO NPCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), and most of these genes were bivalent genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Venn diagram analysis in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Most of the overlapped down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A and Asf1a KO NPCs were bivalent genes.
source: Interestingly, we observed that most of the down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs (62% of total), which represent those genes showing defects in induction compared to WT NPC, were overlapped with the down-regulated genes in Asf1a KO NPCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), and most of these genes were bivalent genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by analysis in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: In both WT and Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs, the H3K27me3 level was reduced compared to their corresponding ESCs.
source: We observed that in both WT and Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs, the H3K27me3 level was reduced compared to their corresponding ESCs, with a modest reduction of H3K27me3 in Mcm2-2A NPCs compared to WT NPCs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 4A.

claim: There was a modest reduction of H3K27me3 in Mcm2-2A NPCs compared to WT NPCs.
source: We observed that in both WT and Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs, the H3K27me3 level was reduced compared to their corresponding ESCs, with a modest reduction of H3K27me3 in Mcm2-2A NPCs compared to WT NPCs (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 4A.

claim: The Mcm2-2A mutation did not have an effect on H3K4me3 levels during differentiation.
source: In contrast, the Mcm2-2A mutation did not have an effect on H3K4me3 levels during differentiation (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Western blot data in Figure 4A.

claim: The effects of Mcm2-2A on the chromatin binding of H3K4me3 or H3K27me3 in ESCs were much less pronounced than that in NPCs.
source: Similar to the transcriptome changes, the effects of Mcm2-2A on the chromatin binding of H3K4me3 or H3K27me3 in ESCs were much less pronounced than that in NPCs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN data in Figure 4B.

claim: Both the reduction of H3K4me3 at the promoter of Pou5f1 and the increase of this mark at the promoter of Pax6 were compromised in Mcm2-2A mutant cells.
source: In Mcm2-2A mutant cells, both the reduction of H3K4me3 at the promoter of Pou5f1 and the increase of this mark at the promoter of Pax6 were compromised, consistent with the compromised silencing of Pou5f1 and the induction of Pax6 in Mcm2-2A mutant cells during differentiation (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN data in Figure 4C.

claim: The average levels of H3K4me3 at the TSS of down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs were significantly lower than those of WT NPCs.
source: Furthermore, the average levels of H3K4me3 at the TSS of down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs were significantly lower than those of WT NPCs and higher at the TSS of up-regulated genes (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN data in Figure 4D.

claim: H3K27me3 density at the TSS of down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs was significantly higher than WT NPCs.
source: On average, H3K27me3 density at the TSS of down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs was significantly higher than WT NPCs.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN data.

claim: H3K27me3 density at the TSS of up-regulated genes was similar between WT and Mcm2-2A NPCs.
source: In contrast, H3K27me3 density at the TSS of up-regulated genes was similar between WT and Mcm2-2A NPCs (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that the reduced expression of genes in Mcm2-2A NPCs likely was due to the retention of this repressive mark during differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN data in Figure 4E.

claim: Using p=0.0001 as a cutoff, 13742 Mcm2 CUT&RUN peaks were identified in WT ESCs.
source: Using p=0.0001 as a cutoff, we identified 13742 Mcm2 CUT&RUN peaks in WT ESCs, demonstrating the reproducibility and reliability of Mcm2 CUT&RUN datasets.
evidence: This is stated in the results and based on CUT&RUN data analysis.

claim: The majority of Mcm2 CUT&RUN peaks were enriched with H3K4me3 CUT&RUN signals and ATAC-seq peaks in ESCs.
source: We observed that the majority of Mcm2 CUT&RUN peaks were enriched with H3K4me3 CUT&RUN signals and ATAC-seq peaks.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN and ATAC-seq data.

claim: Over 26% bivalent domains had at least one Mcm2 peak nearby compared with 21% H3K4me3 peaks having a Mcm2 peak.
source: However, when taking into consideration of total number of H3K4me3, H3K27me3, and bivalent domains in ESCs, we observed that over 26% bivalent domains had at least one Mcm2 peaks nearby compared with 21% H3K4me3 peaks having a Mcm2 peak (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by analysis in Figure 5B.

claim: Almost all the Mcm2 peaks in WT NPCs co-localized with H3K4me3 and ATAC-seq peaks (H3K4me3+, H3K27me3-).
source: We also performed similar analysis on 2686 of Mcm2 peaks identified in WT NPCs and observed that almost all the Mcm2 peaks co-localized with H3K4me3 and ATAC-seq peaks (H3K4me3+, H3K27me3-) (Figure 5A, right).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN and ATAC-seq data in Figure 5A.

claim: Mcm2 CUT&RUN signals were enriched at the TSS of highly transcribed genes compared to the TSS of lowly transcribed genes in both ESCs and NPCs.
source: Moreover, Mcm2 CUT&RUN signals were enriched at the TSS of highly transcribed genes compared to the TSS of lowly transcribed genes in both ESCs and NPCs (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), indicating that the majority of Mcm2 localizes at actively transcribed regions and that Mcm2 may function in gene transcription in a manner independent of its role in DNA replication.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN data in Figure 5C.

claim: Far more reduced Mcm2 CUT&RUN peaks than increased peaks were observed in both Mcm2-2A mutant ESCs and NPCs compared with their WT counterparts.
source: We observed far more reduced Mcm2 CUT&RUN peaks than increased peaks in both Mcm2-2A mutant ESCs and NPCs compared with their WT counterparts (Figure 5D; Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN data in Figure 5D.

claim: Most of the Mcm2 reduced peaks occurred at active promoters and bivalent chromatin regions.
source: Most of these Mcm2 reduced peaks occurred at active promoters and bivalent chromatin regions, whereas increased peaks showed no specific enrichment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by genomic annotation analysis in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The average level of Mcm2-2A density at the TSS of down-regulated genes in ESCs was significantly lower than that in WT ESCs.
source: We found that the average level of Mcm2-2A density at the TSS of down-regulated genes in ESCs was significantly lower than that in WT ESCs, but Mcm2 density at up-regulated genes was similar between WT and Mcm2-2A mutant ESCs (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN data in Figure 5F.

claim: Mcm2 CUT&RUN density in Mcm2-2A mutant ESCs was reduced at the down-regulated genes in NPCs.
source: In addition, Mcm2 CUT&RUN density in Mcm2-2A mutant ESCs was reduced at the down-regulated genes in NPCs (Figure 5H), as exemplified at the promoter of neural lineage gene Pax6, where Mcm2 CUT&RUN density was down-regulated in mutant NPCs compared to WT NPCs (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by CUT&RUN data in Figure 5H.

claim: In ESCs, the Mcm2-2A mutation did not markedly change ATAC-seq profiles.
source: Volcano plot analysis and genome-wide correlation revealed that in ESCs, the Mcm2-2A mutation did not markedly change ATAC-seq profiles (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ATAC-seq data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, C.

claim: ATAC-seq profiles in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs were dramatically altered compared to WT NPCs.
source: In contrast, ATAC-seq profiles in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs were dramatically altered compared to WT NPCs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ATAC-seq data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B, D.

claim: The average level of ATAC-seq signals at the TSS of down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs was significantly lower than WT NPCs.
source: Moreover, the average level of ATAC-seq signals at the TSS of down-regulated genes in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs was significantly lower than WT NPCs. The opposite was true for up-regulated genes (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ATAC-seq data in Figure 6B.

claim: A dramatic reduction of ATAC-seq density was observed at the reduced Mcm2 peak group in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs.
source: We observed a dramatic reduction of ATAC-seq density at the reduced Mcm2 peak group in Mcm2-2A mutant NPCs, along with a slight increase of ATAC-seq density at increased Mcm2 peak groups (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ATAC-seq data in Figure 6C and D.

claim: ATAC-seq signals in Mcm2-2A NPCs at Group 1 and Group 2 Mcm2 peaks were significantly reduced compared to WT NPCs.
source: Importantly, ATAC-seq signals in Mcm2-2A NPCs at Group 1 and Group 2 Mcm2 peaks were significantly reduced compared to WT NPCs, with a larger reduction in Group 1 than in Group 2, whereas ATAC-seq signals in Mcm2-2A NPCs were increased slightly at Group 3 and Group 4 Mcm2 peaks (Figure 6E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by ATAC-seq data in Figure 6E and F.

claim: A reduction of Mcm2 binding in Mcm2-2A mutant ESCs perturbs chromatin changes at bivalent chromatin domains during differentiation.
source: As Mcm2 Group 1 peaks co-localize with bivalent chromatin domains (H3K4me3+ and H3K27me3+), these results indicate that a reduction of Mcm2 binding in Mcm2-2A mutant ESCs, while having little effects on chromatin accessibility in ESCs, perturbs chromatin changes at bivalent chromatin domains during differentiation.
evidence: This is stated in the results and inferred from ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN data.

claim: Mcm2, Pole3, and Pole4 function in the transfer of parental H3-H4 following DNA replication in yeast and mouse ESCs.
source: We and others have previously shown that Mcm2, Pole3, and Pole4, three replisome components first known for their roles in DNA replication, function in the transfer of parental H3-H4 following DNA replication in yeast and mouse ESCs (Gan et al., 2018; Li et al., 2020; Petryk et al., 2018; Xu et al., 2022; Yu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: Mouse ESCs with deletion of Pole3, Pole4, or with mutations at the histone binding motif of Mcm2 (Mcm2-2A) largely grow normally.
source: Remarkably, mouse ESCs with deletion of Pole3, Pole4, or with mutations at the histone binding motif of Mcm2 (Mcm2-2A) largely grow normally.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in the manuscript.

claim: Mcm2-2A mutation in yeast and mouse ESCs has little impacts on the response to replication stress.
source: However, unlike depletion of MCM subunits in these studies, Mcm2-2A mutation in yeast and mouse ESCs has little impacts on the response to replication stress.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and based on previous studies.

claim: It is unlikely that defects in differentiation in Mcm2-2A mutant cells are largely due to its impact on firing of dormant origins.
source: Therefore, it is unlikely that defects in differentiation in Mcm2-2A mutant cells are largely due to its impact on firing of dormant origins.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and inferred from the data and previous studies.

claim: Mcm2, through its interaction with H3-H4, likely regulates differentiation through multiple mechanisms, one of which involves in the resolution of bivalent chromatin domains through its interaction with Asf1a bridged by H3-H4.
source: In summary, our results indicate that Mcm2, through its interaction with H3-H4, likely regulates differentiation through multiple mechanisms, one of which involves in the resolution of bivalent chromatin domains through its interaction with Asf1a bridged by H3-H4.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and summarizes the findings of the study.
